title: Evaluation of well-being and patient satisfaction during procedures under regional anesthesia using the anesthesiological follow-up questionnaire
summary: Both the preoperative expectations of patients regarding the occurrence of possible postoperative symptoms (e.g., pain, nausea and vomiting, reduced alertness, cognitive deficits) and the actual perioperative clinical symptoms are taken into account. On this basis, conclusions should be drawn as to whether patient expectations are related to the symptoms that occurred. In addition, the investigation of symptom intensities is intended to show which postoperative symptoms (for example, pain, nausea and vomiting, impaired memory function, postoperative recovery) are considered relevant by our patients and to identify gender-specific differences within the overall concept. The aim of the study is also to determine whether certain measures can promote empathetic understanding of patients by healthcare providers.Individual approaches should be identified in order to protectively influence the prevalence of anesthesia-related symptoms in the future. Furthermore, detecting negative experiences and memories could provide future protection. To address this more effectively, subjective memory is assessed in detail pre-, peri-, and postoperatively, and a subjective evaluation is collected. Ultimately, the goal of the study is to improve anesthesia quality and patient comfort in the context of regional anesthesia procedures.

interventions.name: Patients included in the study are to fill out a standardized questionnaire by themselves pre- and postoperatively. criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Elective surgeries in orthopedics, trauma/hand surgery, and vascular surgery
• Semi-elective surgeries with marked urgency (N12, N24, N48-72)
• Planned regional anesthesia, possibly in combination with analgesic sedation and/or general anesthesia
• Signed consent to participate
• Consent to anesthesiological measures after an informational consultation
Exclusion criteria:
• Non-consent to participation
• Contraindications for performing regional anesthesia
• Patients not capable of being informed/consenting
• Planned sole general anesthesia
• Unable to independently complete the questionnaires
• Lack of proficiency in the German language
